explain.say: A red blood cell is made in the bone marrow. Before it leaves, it throws out its nucleus, leaving more room for haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen.

explain.say: For about four months it travels round and round the body, loading oxygen in the lungs and squeezing through capillaries narrower than itself to deliver it. All that squeezing wears it out.

explain.say: Old, stiff cells are caught and eaten in the spleen and liver. The iron is saved to make new red cells, and the rest of the haemoglobin is broken down. Meanwhile the marrow makes millions of new cells every second.

faq.q: How long does a red blood cell live?
faq.a: A red blood cell lives for about 120 days, roughly four months. In that time it travels round the body many thousands of times.
asks: What is the lifespan of a red blood cell?

faq.q: Why don't red blood cells have a nucleus?
faq.a: Mature human red blood cells push out their nucleus as they form. This leaves more space for haemoglobin, but it also means they cannot repair themselves, which is why they only live about four months.
asks: Do red blood cells have DNA?
What is inside a red blood cell?

faq.q: What happens to old red blood cells?
faq.a: Worn-out red blood cells become stiff and get trapped in the spleen and liver, where white blood cells called macrophages eat them. Their iron is recycled to make new red blood cells.
asks: Where do dead blood cells go?

faq.q: How many red blood cells does the body make?
faq.a: The bone marrow makes about 2 to 3 million new red blood cells every second, replacing the ones that wear out.
asks: How fast does the body make blood?
Where are red blood cells made?

faq.q: Why are red blood cells shaped like doughnuts?
faq.a: Their dimpled disc shape gives a large surface for oxygen to pass in and out, and makes them flexible enough to fold and squeeze through the narrowest capillaries.
asks: What shape are red blood cells?
Why are red blood cells flexible?

facts: Red blood cells live for about 120 days.
The body makes roughly 2 to 3 million red blood cells every second.
An adult has roughly 25 trillion red blood cells, making them the most numerous cells in the body.

quiz.say: Why does a red blood cell only live about four months?
quiz.show: Red blood cells wear out after about 120 days because…

options.show: They have no nucleus to repair themselves
options.say: They have no nucleus to repair themselves

quiz.why: Without a nucleus they cannot make new proteins to repair damage, so they gradually wear out and are recycled.

wrong.1: They load fresh oxygen every lap through the lungs.
wrong.2: Old red cells are removed by the body's own macrophages, not germs.
